note: Sealed before the measured N=10 run. Bars are set from an N=2 trial on the same stack (test:801, test:802) with roughly 50% headroom on each per-operation p90, because N=2 cannot see queueing at one sbx-worker replica. Falsified predictions are reported, not rewritten.

predictions.claim: Every one of the 10 users completes all six operations with no failure.
run_id p90 stays under 4500 ms. This is the first command in a fresh sandbox and the one most exposed to contention at a single worker.
run_uname p90 stays under 4000 ms, and its p50 is at or below run_id's: the second run in the same sandbox meets a warmer path.
Ten concurrent users cost far less than ten sequential ones: wall clock stays under 30000 ms, against roughly 89000 ms for the same work run one user after another at the N=2 per-user total.
The driver runs on a free-threaded interpreter, so the N threads are genuinely concurrent.
